scenarios.name: cheat
scenarios.title: Cheating seller
scenarios.blurb: Tidewater ships a junk export under the contracted file name: a renamed column, 312 rows and reused order ids. The hash fails, the arbiter cites the contract and voids the escrow.

scenarios.name: partial
scenarios.title: Partial delivery
scenarios.blurb: Tidewater ships the file it committed to, but 500 of its 5,000 rows fail Northwind's row checks. The contract carries a signed pro-rata term, so Trustee captures the valid 90% ($140.40 of $156.00) and releases the rest to Northwind.

scenarios.name: forged
scenarios.title: Impostor seller
scenarios.blurb: Someone who is not Tidewater signs the contract as Tidewater. Trustee checks the signature against the registered key, refuses before any money moves, and PayPal is never called.

scenarios.name: a2a
scenarios.title: Three A2A agents
scenarios.blurb: Northwind's planning agent and Tidewater's sales agent are real A2A agents, each with its own Agent Card and JSON-RPC endpoint. They find each other by card, negotiate over A2A with signed offers, countersign the contract and open the escrow at Trustee, which holds the money. Tidewater ships when Trustee pushes "funds held".

scenarios.name: overreach
scenarios.title: Agent over-reaches its instruction
scenarios.blurb: The human told the agent to spend at most $175. Tidewater will not go below $190 and the agent's own budget would allow it. Trustee checks the signed intent, sees the price is outside it, and refuses to pay unattended: the purchase steps up to a human approval.
